# Follow-up question bank

Use these as prompts, not as a script. Rewrite every question so that it names something concrete
from the current source (a fact id, a section, a scene time). Give each a default. Mark blockers `[blocking]`.

## intake
- Who is the primary viewer (role, seniority, prior knowledge), and what should they do after the video?
- What runtime and pace? [default: 3:00 at 150 wpm]
- Presenter on screen, named presenter as voice-over, or anonymous voice-over? [default: voice-over]
- Which sections are mandatory (pain points, value proposition, use cases, call to action, other)?
- Which call-to-action options may be offered, and which contact details or booking link may be shown?
- Does the source have a sensitivity or confidentiality level that limits what may be shown?

## ingest
- Is this the final version of the source, or is there a newer one? [blocking if the date looks old]
- The extraction found N words and M sections. Does that match what you expected?
- Are there parts of the source to exclude (appendix, legal text, comments, footers)?
- If a page or PDF was thin: can you provide a DOCX or TXT export?
- Is the source's author or publisher to be credited on screen?

## facts
- Which of the top 5 facts matter most to this audience? Which should be dropped?
- Gap G1 (source does not say X): leave out, mark illustrative, or provide the fact?
- Fact F-n is a claim with a number: may it be shown as-is, or does it need a citation on screen?
- Which product, brand or competitor names may be used on screen?
- Which terms need a specific spoken form?

## structure
- Does the section map cover every mandatory section? Merge, split or reorder anything?
- Is the time split right (for example 1:10 problem, 2:10 demo, 0:40 use cases, 0:40 call to action)?
- Should the demo be one continuous story or several short vignettes?
- Which section may be cut first if the runtime must shrink by 20 %?

## script
- Tone: confident, warm, technical, humorous? Any phrases to avoid or require?
- Scene N states claim C. Is the wording acceptable to legal or marketing?
- Which visuals are real captures and which are rendered illustrations?
- Should the on-screen text be translated or localised?
- Do you want a shorter cut-down (for example 60 s) as a later option?

## validate
- Scene N is tight by X seconds. Shorten the voice-over, extend the window, or lower the pace?
- Runtime is Y s against a target of Z s. Trim scene A or extend scene B?
- Warnings remain (list). Accept them or fix them?

## plan
- Which recording or visual approach: real screen capture, rendered mock-ups, stock footage, slides?
- Voice: which synthetic voice, or a human recording? Which language?
- Who reviews the video before it is published, and by when?
- Any brand assets (logo, colours, template) to use?

## approval
- Approve as is, approve with changes (list them), or revise?
- Placeholders still open: list them. Provide them now or ship with placeholders?
- Where should the final assets be stored, and who gets the outcome record?

## production
- The audio stage extended scenes N and M. Shorten the voice-over, lower the pace, or accept the longer runtime?
- Review frames: which scenes need a different look before the full render?
- Generic storyboard cards or a story-specific renderer for this video?
- Where should the final MP4 and SRT be stored, and who reviews and publishes them?
- Re-render only after a script change (new version and new approval), or fix a voice or pace setting first?

## Quality bar
- Specific beats generic ("Fact F4 gives 38 files; show the number on screen?" beats "Any changes?").
- At most 5 per step. One decision per question. A default for every question.
